title: Merge Adjacent Equal Elements
summary: Given an integer array nums, repeatedly apply the following operation until no more changes can be made: - If any two adjacent elements are equal, replace them with a single element equal to their sum.
statement: Given an integer array nums, repeatedly apply the following operation until no more changes can be made: - If any two adjacent elements are equal, replace them with a single element equal to their sum. - Continue this process on the updated array until no adjacent equal elements remain. Return the final array after all possible merge operations.
constraints: nums contains between 1 and 100,000 positive integers.
Scan from left to right; merging a pair can immediately create another equal pair with its new left neighbor.
Return the stable sequence after all such cascading merges.
hints: The unresolved suffix is the only place where a new equality can appear.
Use a stack and repeatedly combine its last two values while they match.
Push each input value, then cascade merges before reading the next value.
Everything below the stack top was already stable; each merge reduces length, so the final stack is exactly the prescribed left-to-right process.
editorial: Everything below the stack top was already stable; each merge reduces length, so the final stack is exactly the prescribed left-to-right process.

tests.explanation: The two ones form two; that two merges with the following two, leaving [3,4].
The ones become two, then the two twos become four, so the answer is [4].
